title: RULES ON INTERNATIONAL JUDICIAL MUTUAL ASSISTANCE IN CIVIL MATTERS
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of these Rules is to prescribe matters necessary for the enforcement of the Act on International Judicial Cooperation in Civil Matters (hereinafter referred to as the "Act").

Article 2 (Recipients of Requests for Judicial Cooperation) In cases under Article 5 of the Act, where a person to be served with documents or examined as a witness resides in the United States of America, a request for judicial cooperation may be addressed to the Ambassador, Minister, or Consul of the Republic of Korea stationed in the United States of America, even if that person is not a national of the Republic of Korea.

Article 3 (Statement of Expenses for Judicial Cooperation)
(1) Where a party has paid in advance the expenses prescribed in Article 9 of the Act, the head of the court to which the presiding judge seeking judicial cooperation belongs shall state that fact in a request for transmission under Article 6 (1) of the Act.
(2) The Director General of the National Court Administration shall state in a request for transmission under Article 6 (2) of the Act that the requesting court will collect from the party concerned an amount equivalent to expenses paid or advanced by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade or an overseas diplomatic or consular mission for service of documents or examination of evidence, and pay it into the National Treasury. <Amended on June 28, 2002>

Article 4 (Reimbursement of Actual Expenses of Judicial Cooperation)
(1) When forwarding documents concerning the result of a request for judicial cooperation, the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Trade or the head of an overseas diplomatic or consular mission shall attach a statement detailing expenses paid or advanced for service or examination of evidence. <Amended on June 28, 2002>
(2) On receiving the statement of expenses under paragraph (1), the requesting court shall, without delay, send an order to release money held in court custody to the cash officer responsible for cash held outside budgetary revenues and expenditures so that the equivalent amount may be transferred from the advance deposit under Article 9 of the Act to the National Treasury. <Amended on June 28, 2002>
(3) Where the expenses in paragraph (2) are denominated in a foreign currency, the amount to be transferred to the National Treasury shall be converted into Korean won at the midpoint of the foreign-exchange buying and selling rates prevailing on the date of transfer.

Article 5 (Channel for Replies concerning Execution of Requests) Article 6 of the Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the channel for returning the result of executing a request by the requested court and to the channel for claims for reimbursement of expenses under Article 7.

Article 6 (Preservation of Records of Execution of Requests)
(1) The requested court shall retain, together with a copy of the reply, those portions of records prepared in connection with the execution of a request received from a foreign country that have not been forwarded to the foreign court under Article 16 (1) of the Act.
(2) The retention period for the documents under paragraph (1) shall be two years. <Amended on June 28, 2002>

Article 7 (Disbursement of Expenses and Claims for Reimbursement)
(1) Where expenses are incurred in executing a request, the requested court shall disburse them against an advance payment from the National Treasury: Provided, That fees and other expenses payable to an enforcement officer may be collected from a foreign institution and paid to the enforcement officer. <Amended on June 28, 2002>
(2) In cases under paragraph (1), the head of the requested court shall forward the statement of expenses and a notice of payment prepared by the court's officer responsible for claims management, or a claim prepared by the enforcement officer, to the Director General of the National Court Administration together with the documents reporting the execution of the request under Article 16 (1) of the Act. <Amended on June 28, 2002>
(3) The Director General of the National Court Administration shall forward the statement of expenses and notice of payment or the claim under paragraph (2) to the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Trade, and request that the Minister arrange for the relevant expenses to be paid to the requested court. <Amended on June 28, 2002>

ADDENDUM <No. 1165, June 14, 1991>
These Rules shall enter into force on the date of their promulgation.

ADDENDUM <No. 1770, June 28, 2002>
These Rules shall enter into force on July 1, 2002.
